memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "These were the heads of their families: The sons of Reuben the firstborn son of Israel were Hanok and Pallu, Hezron and Karmi. These were the clans of Reuben. The sons of Simeon were Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jakin, Zohar and Shaul the son of a Canaanite woman. These were the clans of Simeon." - Exodus 6:14-15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Right in the middle of a dramatic confrontation with Pharaoh, the narrative pauses for a family register. It feels like an interruption. Why here?

Because God is establishing that this deliverance happens to a real family, with real names, in real history. Israel is not a symbol. These are people with fathers and grandfathers, and God knows every one of them.

We know almost nothing about Hanok, Pallu, Hezron or Karmi. They did nothing famous. Yet their names sit permanently in the Word of God. That should encourage anyone who feels their life is too ordinary to matter.

Notice one small detail — Shaul, the son of a Canaanite woman. She was an outsider, and Scripture records her son without shame. God's people have always included those who came in from outside. That thread runs all the way to Rahab and Ruth, and into the genealogy of Jesus Himself (Mt 1:5).

You may never be famous. You are not anonymous to God.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I believe my ordinary life is fully known and valued by God?
2. Am I as welcoming to outsiders as God has been?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You know my name and my family. Help me to welcome those the world would leave out. Amen.
